headline: High risk of data leakage and cascading errors: open-webui’s broad network/MCP/file access can amplify caveman’s content-writing outputs into unsafe downstream actions.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: open-webui can use MCP, plugins, and tool servers, so it may ingest caveman outputs through shared channels; caveman also touches CLAUDE.md and project notes, which are plausible instruction-bearing files. No direct shared channel is documented, so this is inferred and uncertainty pushes upward from low.
conditions: IF caveman writes instructions into shared files that open-webui reads as prompts, injection is possible.
IF open-webui is configured to pass caveman-generated text into MCP or tool calls without provenance checks, hijack risk increases.
mitigations: Disable shared-file ingestion between the agents.
Require provenance tags on any caveman-generated text before open-webui consumes it.
Restrict open-webui MCP/tool access to allowlisted servers only.
Review and sanitize CLAUDE.md and project notes before reuse.
requires-engineering: add content-isolation or sandbox boundaries between the two agents.

B_data_leakage.rationale: caveman touches session logs, memory files, project notes, and CLAUDE.md, while open-webui handles files, persistent memory, API keys, and broad network egress. If they share a workspace or mounted volume, sensitive data can flow from caveman into open-webui and then out via networked APIs. The pairwise leakage path is plausible in default deployments.
conditions: IF both agents can read the same directory or mounted volume, caveman data can be exposed to open-webui.
IF open-webui is connected to external APIs while holding shared files or memory, leakage can leave the local environment.
mitigations: Separate the agents onto different workspaces or volumes.
Remove secrets and session logs from any shared directory.
Disable external API connectors in open-webui for shared-data runs.
Rotate any API keys that may have been present in open-webui memory.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent storage isolation and egress policy controls.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: caveman supports multiple instances and file access, while open-webui supports multiple instances, persistent shared sessions, and mounted data volumes. That creates overlapping write surfaces on shared state, especially if both are pointed at the same files or session-backed resources. No locking is documented, so conflict risk is real but not necessarily catastrophic.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same project files or mounted volume, last-writer-wins conflicts can occur.
IF open-webui shares Redis-backed session state across workers while caveman edits related files, state divergence is possible.
mitigations: Assign separate write directories to each agent.
Turn off concurrent edits during shared tasks.
Use file locks or a single-writer workflow for shared artifacts.
Snapshot shared files before running both agents.
requires-engineering: add transactional coordination for shared mutable resources.

D_cascading_error.rationale: open-webui can act on tool outputs and broad APIs, while caveman is a content-writing agent that can generate persuasive but unverified text. If open-webui treats caveman output as authoritative, errors can cascade into browser actions, API calls, or published content. The interaction is plausible by default and can cause irreversible downstream mistakes.
conditions: IF open-webui forwards caveman-generated text into tools without verification, false claims can become actions.
IF caveman produces instructions or summaries that open-webui publishes or executes, downstream harm can propagate.
mitigations: Require human review before any tool action based on caveman output.
Add a verification step that checks caveman claims against sources.
Disable autonomous browser or subprocess actions for shared workflows.
Mark caveman output as untrusted in open-webui prompts.
requires-engineering: implement structured provenance and validation gates.

E_compliance.rationale: caveman touches session logs, memory files, project notes, and CLAUDE.md, while open-webui handles persistent memory, usage analytics, files, and API keys. If regulated or sensitive data is placed into open-webui, its broader networked integrations and analytics can create retention or residency mismatches. The profiles do not specify a concrete jurisdiction mismatch, so medium is the highest supportable level.
conditions: IF regulated data is stored in open-webui persistent memory or analytics, retention obligations may be violated.
IF shared files contain jurisdiction-bound data and open-webui sends them to external APIs, residency controls may fail.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of open-webui memory and analytics.
Disable external connectors for compliance-sensitive runs.
Purge shared logs after each session.
Restrict API-key use to non-sensitive workflows.
requires-engineering: add residency, retention, and deletion controls per data class.
